bill.name: Engaging Next-generation Leaders in Information about Service and Training Act (ENLIST Act; H.R. 2781)
bill.status: Introduced in House · Kiggans / Panetta · referred to House Armed Services on 2025-04-09
bill.analyzed: Full introduced-in-House bill (2 pages; §§1–2), with §2 as the sole substantive provision.

sourceLimits: The supplied 1,195-byte, 194-word raw source contains the bill's sole substantive amendment as flattened one-line text, has no page boundaries or metadata sidecar, and omits the standard enacting clause visible in the official PDF. The official Congress.gov introduced-version PDF establishes the two-page count, and Congress.gov establishes the current introduced status. Section 2 amends 10 U.S.C. §503(c)(1)(A) by cross-reference without reproducing the chapeau, covered-entity definition, private-school exception, existing recruiting-access process, or enforcement and reporting provisions; the codified section was also amended after this bill was introduced. The current U.S. Code was consulted only to identify that surrounding structure, not to infer a count of covered schools or implementation activity. The bill does not specify whether or where each covered school must display the information, define the required information, say who supplies or updates it, state placement, format, duration, or accessibility standards, provide an effective date, implementation deadline, or funding, or create a display-specific inspection, complaint, enforcement, or public-reporting mechanism. It states no awareness, application, enlistment, or other measurable downstream target. No named recurring official compliance series was identified; on the sources reviewed, a nationwide count or share of compliant schools would require a bespoke audit. Aggregate military recruiting or accession data would neither measure compliance nor isolate this clause's effect. No defensible automatically resolvable metric or empirical conditional was verified, so metrics and conditionals are empty and no series hints or stance matrices are supplied.

provisions.title: Section 2 — Display of military-recruiting information at certain secondary schools
provisions.heading: §2: Add an affirmative school-hours display and accessibility duty
provisions.quote: “(iv) shall display and make accessible to students, during school hours, information regarding military recruiting.”
provisions.context: Section 1 supplies only the short title. Section 2 is the bill's sole substantive provision. It changes the period at the end of 10 U.S.C. §503(c)(1)(A)(iii) to “; and” and adds clause (iv), which directs the local educational agencies covered by the referenced paragraph to display and make military-recruiting information accessible to students during school hours. The punctuation edit has no independent policy effect; it connects the existing clauses to the new duty. The referenced statutory chapeau, definitions, exemptions, and existing access-enforcement sequence are not reproduced in the bill. The new clause contains no recruiter-request trigger, effective date, implementation deadline, information specification, placement or format rule, update cadence, funding, display-specific verification process, reporting duty, or measurable recruiting outcome.
goals: Require the educational agencies covered by 10 U.S.C. §503(c)(1)(A) to display and make information regarding military recruiting accessible to students during school hours.

effects.text: Upon enactment, the covered educational agencies would have an affirmative duty to display military-recruiting information and make it accessible to students during school hours; the text does not make that duty contingent on a recruiter's request.

A compliant display could create an additional opportunity for students to encounter recruiting information, but the bill would not require any student to view the information, contact a recruiter, apply, or enlist.
Because the clause sets no content, medium, placement, duration, or updating standard, implementations could differ materially while each could arguably satisfy the sparse statutory text.

barriers.text: The bill supplies no implementation lead time or funding and leaves the required content, supplier, medium, placement, accessibility standard, hours of availability, and update responsibility unspecified.

barriers.actor: Department of Defense and statutory enforcement officials
barriers.text: The surrounding statute escalates denials of requested recruiting access through meetings and notifications, while new clause (iv) is not expressly request-triggered. The bill does not explain how a failure to display would enter that process or which official would verify it.

The bill creates no display-specific inspection, complaint, data-collection, or public-reporting requirement, and no named recurring official product was identified from which nationwide compliance could be resolved.
